prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” lawyer for every truck crash — the best choice depends on your case details (severity of injuries, whether death occurred, who the defendants are), whether you want a trial-tested litigator, and practical things like communication style and fee terms. I can help you find strong candidates, but first here’s how to identify the right Dallas attorney and what to do next.

How to pick the right Dallas truck‑accident attorney
- Look for trucking-specific experience: commercial vehicle cases involve Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) rules, driver logs, employer vicarious liability, and insurance/indemnity issues. Choose a lawyer who regularly handles truck accidents, not just car crashes.
- Trial experience and verdicts: trucking companies and big insurers often won’t settle unless they know you have a lawyer who will try the case. Ask about jury verdicts and high-value settlements in truck cases.
- Resources and team: trucking cases often require depositions, expert witnesses (accident reconstruction, life care planners, vocational experts), and forensic review of ELD/GPS data — make sure the firm has the budget and staff to pursue that.
- Board certification & peer recognition: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (if applicable), AV Preeminent (Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers, Million Dollar Advocates Forum are helpful indicators.
- Communication and accessibility: ask how often you’ll get updates, who you contact, and who will actually handle your case.
- Fee structure: most personal-injury firms work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Confirm the percentage, how costs are advanced and repaid, and whether the percentage changes if you settle vs. go to trial.

Key questions to ask during a free consultation
- How many truck accident cases have you handled in Dallas/Fort Worth? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases against trucking companies and their insurers? Any experience with FMCSA compliance evidence (ELD, driver logs, maintenance records)?
- What were some results (settlements/verdicts) in truck cases?
- Who will work on my case day‑to‑day? Will you use experts? Which ones?
- What is your contingency fee and how are costs handled?
- What is the case strategy and estimated timeline?
- Do you have client references?

Red flags to avoid
- No truck-specific experience or inability to explain FMCSA/ELD/logs issues.
- Unwillingness to take the case to trial or vague answers about prior trial experience.
- Pushy “quick settlement” pressure before reviewing medical records.
- No written fee agreement or unclear cost advance policy.

Immediate steps you should take now (if you haven’t already)
- Seek prompt medical care and keep all records and bills.
- Preserve evidence: photos, dashcam/phone video, vehicle damage, contact info for witnesses, police report number.
- Don’t sign or give a recorded statement to an insurer before talking to an attorney.
- Save phone records/texts related to the crash; preserve your phone and vehicle event data.
- Note deadlines: Texas generally has a 2‑year statute of limitations for personal injury and wrongful death (act promptly).

Where to find reputable Dallas truck‑accident lawyers
- Use multiple sources: Dallas Bar Association lawyer referral, Texas Trial Lawyers Association, Martindale-Hubbell AV ratings, Super Lawyers, local plaintiffs’ firms’ truck-accident practice pages, and client reviews. Contact 3–4 firms for initial free consults and compare answers.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short list of specific Dallas law firms/attorneys to contact (if you allow me to look up current info), or
- Provide a short script and list of the exact questions to ask during initial consultations, or
- Review intake answers from firms you’ve already contacted and help you compare them.

Tell me which you prefer and a few case details (date of crash, injuries, fatalities, whether police report is filed, whether the truck company or insurer has contacted you) and I’ll help you next.
